$comment: Hand-written engineering log for /testing, in public language: what was tested, what was seen, what changed. No names, tools, suppliers, prices or datasheet figures. sync-testing.mjs validates it and copies published entries into public/testing/index.json. figureId must name a published figure.

items.tested: Thrust map at 16:48 UTC on one 6S pack: ten throttle holds from 10 to 100 percent, with the abort on bus loss in place.
items.saw: Thrust reached 1652 g at 31283 rpm at 100 percent throttle. The pack read 23.9 V at rest and the ESC temperature stayed live, 38 to 53 C. The load cell zero moved by 2 g before and 0.5 g after the run. A capture at 16:35 UTC had a zero drift of up to 27 g and an ESC temperature frozen by a pack swap, so its thrust offsets and temperatures are not used.
items.changed: The bench software was fixed so the ESC temperature stays live after a pack swap.

items.tested: Thrust map on the new thrust stand: ten throttle holds from 10 to 100 percent.
items.saw: In the 13:25 UTC run thrust reached 1496 g at 100 percent throttle on the OpenMotor-2306. In the earlier 13:16 UTC run the operator unplugged the pack during the 80 percent step because of the noise, and the throttle profile kept stepping up to full with no pack connected.
items.changed: The bench controller now aborts the run when the bus voltage disappears under command. The 13:25 UTC run was recorded with that change. The thrust stand test plans no longer include a current cut, because current sense on the stand is not calibrated.

items.tested: Continuous current rating by stepping to a fixed current and waiting for the die temperature to settle.
items.saw: Calculated from the fitted thermal time constant of 5 to 10 minutes, not captured: a fixed-current step on a pack cannot reach thermal steady state, because 20 s at the target current gives only a few percent of the steady temperature rise.
items.changed: The bench now holds a target die temperature and reads the current needed to hold it.

items.tested: Review of the scope captures from the destructive ramp session.
items.saw: Scope channel 1 read one constant value in all nine sessions of that afternoon and no check flagged it.

items.tested: Throttle sweep against a clamp reference.
items.saw: The current-sense amplifier reading, as read by the bench controller, did not track the clamp: 11.6 A against 32.4 A at 80 percent throttle, and 64.7 A against 55.7 A at 100 percent.
items.changed: An input network was added to the current-sense amplifier in rev3.2. It has not been tested on hardware: no capture after the change exists.

items.tested: One channel ramped from 0 to full throttle with no thermal guard.
items.saw: Clamp current peaked at 39.8 A with the die sensor at 156 C. The die reading reached 161 C and bus voltage telemetry then stopped.

items.tested: First boards flashed for the bench.
items.saw: Boards left the flashing step with the temperature limit at 255 and a default motor preset.
items.changed: Both are now set per product in the flashing jig.

items.tested: First flights of the full stack on five drones.
items.saw: 103 blackbox logs from four of the drones, about half of them arm and disarm blips. The fifth drone's SD card failed after the session. On the 8 inch, seven logs were recorded with the FC on a separate battery, so their voltage is not pack voltage.

items.tested: Ride out to 5.3 km with a Gemini and a Mono on the same carry.
items.saw: Beyond 2.9 km the Gemini's reported RSSI was below the Mono's in 24 of the 25 100 m bins and equal in one, by a median of 4 dB and up to 7 dB. Its link quality was higher in all 25 bins, by a median of 15 points. The log numbers its receivers instead of naming them, so the column-to-unit mapping was taken from the operators' notes and one duplicate column was excluded.
